capacity.daemon_dir: %s is a daemon's state directory (it has %s)
capacity.dir_in_use: %s is a state directory in use, not a throwaway one
capacity.dir_not_empty: %s is not empty; the drill fills only a directory made for it
capacity.failed: result    FAILED: the row did not go ok → warn → critical → full, act (%s) exactly once and produce exactly one notice
capacity.flag.dir: a throwaway state directory, empty or not there yet (default: a new temporary one)
capacity.flag.drill: the row to fill on purpose:
capacity.flag.keep: leave the directory behind to look at
capacity.flag.limit: the limit to run the row at; it may only be lower than the register's (default: 4KiB for a row of bytes, 20 for a row of rows)
capacity.more_notices: (%s; %d more held back by the one-a-day rule)
capacity.no_drill: clawdline: %s has no drill; the rows with one are: %s
capacity.usage: usage: clawdline doctor capacity --drill <%s> [--dir D] [--limit N] [--keep]
capacity.wrote: wrote     %d times through the row's own writer
devices.empty: nothing is signed in to this machine but this machine itself
devices.flag.json: print the daemon's answer as it is
devices.own_key: this command uses this machine's own key, which is not listed and is not revoked here
devices.password: a password is set: whoever knows it can sign in another device
devices.revoke_prompt: Revoke %s (%s)? Whatever is signed in with it — this browser too, if it is the one — is refused from its next request. [y/N]
devices.unknown_id: clawdline: no device signed in to this machine has the id %s (see `clawdline devices`)
devices.unreadable: the daemon's answer could not be read: %w
devices.usage.cloud: browsers reached through Clawdline Cloud are `clawdline cloud devices`
devices.usage.direct: the browsers and devices signed in to this machine directly (clawdline open, pairing, password);
update.bundle_instructions: clawdline: --apply does not replace an app bundle; run these from a source checkout:
update.fetch_failed: clawdline: git fetch origin main failed: %v
update.flag.apply: deploy the latest build (Linux, inside a source checkout)
update.flag.force: with --apply: deploy even when this machine is current or ahead
update.latest_unknown: clawdline: the cloud's latest build is not known, so there is nothing to apply
update.linux_only: clawdline: --apply is built for Linux only, not %s (docs/updates.md)
update.no_deploy_script: clawdline: --apply runs inside a Clawdline source checkout; %s has no tools/deploy-linux-user.sh
update.not_checkout: clawdline: --apply runs inside a Clawdline source checkout, and this directory is not one
update.nothing_to_apply: clawdline: this machine is %s; nothing to apply (--force deploys %s anyway)
update.refuse_unmerged: clawdline: %s is not on origin/main; refusing to deploy it
usage.baseline_exists: %s already holds a frozen baseline; name another with --out
usage.baseline_too_large: %s is larger than a frozen baseline can be
usage.causality: units are not assigned to periods at random: this says what changed, not why.
usage.definition_mismatch_daemon: clawdline usage: the daemon reads definition %d and the baseline was frozen with %d; freeze a new baseline with this daemon
usage.definition_mismatch_file: %s was frozen with definition %d and this build reads %d
usage.empty: no unit of work in either period
usage.froze: froze %d units (%d with no whole reading) created %s – %s, definition %d, to %s
usage.frozen_truncated: truncated: the range held more tasks than one answer reads; only the newest are frozen
usage.met_needs: met needs, in a group with enough units: cache-read median down at least 30%%, duration p75 up at most 10%%, no guardrail rate worse.
usage.overlap: the trial starts before the baseline ends: some units may be in both periods
usage.period_truncated: %s truncated: the range held more tasks than one answer reads; only the newest are in it
usage.periods: baseline: %d units created %s – %s; trial: %d units created %s – %s
usage.unreadable: the daemon's answer could not be read
